page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.gn8v-4x.8xlarge is an accelerator-optimized virtual server hosted on the KVM hypervisor using the x86_64 architecture. The system is provisioned with 32 dedicated vCPUs from the Intel Xeon 8469C processor series operating at a base clock speed of 2.6 GHz. Memory resources are configured at 384.0 GB of system RAM, establishing an allocation of 12.0 GB per vCPU. This high memory-to-vCPU ratio ensures ample capacity for processing data-dense workloads directly in memory without CPU-level memory starvation.

Acceleration capabilities are anchored by four integrated GPUs providing an aggregate of 384 GB of video memory. In terms of connectivity, the instance delivers a baseline network throughput of 20 Gbps, facilitating rapid inter-node communication or network-based data transfers. Local disk storage is not bundled with this configuration, which directs all persistent and scratch storage requirements to cloud-attached block storage interfaces. Complimentary public IPv4 addresses are not included with the virtual instance.

The architectural design prioritizes high accelerator density and expansive GPU and system memory over onboard storage. For workloads bounded by VRAM and parallel calculation throughput, this consolidation delivers high computational efficiency relative to allocating multiple smaller GPU instances. The primary tradeoff lies in the dependence on network-attached storage for disk operations, making baseline network management critical for IOPS-heavy jobs. The instance is structured for distributed machine learning training, large-scale deep learning model fine-tuning, complex computer vision tasks, high-concurrency neural network inference, and parallel scientific simulations.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.gn8v-4x.8xlarge is a GPU-accelerated compute instance powered by the KVM hypervisor and built on the x86_64 architecture. The server provides 32 dedicated vCPUs running on Intel Xeon 8469C processors with a base frequency of 2.6 GHz, coupled with 384 GB of system memory, yielding 12 GB of memory per core. Hardware acceleration is provided by four onboard GPUs that deliver a combined 384 GB of video memory. Network performance is provisioned with a 20 Gbps baseline bandwidth, while internal persistent disks are absent, requiring workloads to rely on remote block storage solutions. The hardware balance emphasizes parallel acceleration alongside substantial host and accelerator memory capacity. This configuration makes the instance suitable for distributed deep learning, large-scale machine learning model training, high-capacity inference pipelines, and parallel scientific simulation workloads requiring substantial memory per virtual processing unit.
